slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The essay's country table states that the e-SIRCEV electronic civil registration system was deployed to 121 of 164 registries by 2021, citing an EMURGO blog; it says deployed, not registering.

The essay's country table states that first capture at rural registry offices still largely uses paper forms before digital entry, with declaration vouchers from health centres or village chiefs entered in paper registers at municipal civil status offices; it gives no date, so the essay's date is used.
facts.system: Municipal civil status offices' paper registers

facts.fact: The essay's country table states that in August 2025 ANIP launched a one-stop digital birth registration pilot in 10 health facilities, including the hospitals at Natitingou and Djougou.
The essay's country table states that in the August 2025 one-stop pilot the data go directly into the RNPP, with the personal identification number generated automatically.

systems.system: Municipal civil status offices' paper registers
systems.tiers: municipal civil status offices, fed by declaration vouchers from health centres or village chiefs

systems.owner: ANIP; given by the World Bank's WURI project
systems.tiers: 2,050 terminals received in October 2024, for birth registration at health facilities in all districts into the RNPP and RNEC

systems.system: National Register of Civil Status Events (RNEC)

systems.tiers: 10.5 million civil status and identity documents issued in 2025, 75% of procedures through digital channels (37% web, 30% app, 8% USSD)
